title: Console tab title may revert to the bare product name after in-app navigation: `BrandingSync` rewrites `document.title` on every route change, `AppShell` only on title change
body:
Found while implementing objectui#6872 (a sweep of every `document.title` writer in the repository); it is outside that card's scope, whose file surface is `packages/layout/src/AppShell.tsx`. Unclaimed. Filed by the objectui#6872 dispatch seat, session `session_01YBWFb5YgMU5dw8p2VKj16S`, on `origin/main` at `c4326fe0a`.

## Facts (static reading, line numbers as of `c4326fe0a` — re-locate by content)

Two independent writers set the console's tab title, keyed on different inputs:

1. `apps/console/src/App.tsx`, `BrandingSync` (about line 132): a `useEffect` keyed on `useLocation()` runs `document.title = getProductName()` — the bare product name — on **every route change**. It is rendered as a sibling **before** `ConsoleShell` inside `BrowserRouter` (about line 166). Its own comment says: "Syncs document title + favicon with runtime branding on every route change."

2. `packages/app-shell/src/layout/ConsoleLayout.tsx` (about lines 168-178) passes `title: LABEL — PRODUCT` (the app label joined to `getProductName()`) into `AppShell`'s `branding`, and `packages/layout/src/AppShell.tsx` `useAppShellBranding` writes `document.title = title` inside an effect whose dependency list ends in `title` — so it fires only when the **composed string changes**, not on navigation.

## Mechanism (not yet measured at runtime)

On the commit where the app first renders, React runs sibling effects in tree order: `BrandingSync` writes the bare product name first, then the shell subtree's effect writes `LABEL — PRODUCT`, and the composed title wins. On a later navigation **inside the same app**, `location` changes but the composed title does not: only writer 1 fires, and the tab would read the bare product name until something changes the composed title again.

## What was and was not measured

- Measured: the three code sites above, by reading `origin/main`; the sweep that found them (`git grep -nE 'document\.title\s*='` over all tracked files: 5 writer files under `apps/console`, 1 under `packages/layout`, 0 elsewhere; lit control `document.documentElement` fired 17 files under `packages/*/src/*`).
- Not measured: no browser run. No existing test pins either behaviour — `apps/console/src/__tests__/runtimeConfigBootDedup.test.ts` pins only the boot-time product name (`expect(document.title).toBe('Acme Ops')`), before any app shell mounts.

## Suggested scope

Measure first: boot the console, open an app, navigate between two of its pages, read the tab title after each step. If the reset is real, decide which writer owns the tab title once a shell is mounted (candidates: key `BrandingSync` on the branding values rather than on `location`; or have `ConsoleLayout` re-apply its composed title on `location`). Nothing in objectui#6872 depends on this, and its PR deliberately does not touch it.

Related: objectui#6872 (documentation fix on the `AppShell` side of this pair; that PR pins that `AppShell` assigns `document.title` wholesale, which is the behaviour writer 2 relies on).
